title: Ethiopian Fish Soup
community: Ethiopian lake communities — the restorative fish broth
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Fish Soup — fish simmered with onion, garlic, turmeric, ginger, and coriander into a light, restorative broth. The fasting-period healing soup — lighter and more gently spiced than fish wat, serving as both a soup and a source of protein.
longDesc: Asa Shorba is the gentle healing soup of Ethiopia's lake communities — the freshwater fish simmered with turmeric and ginger into a golden broth of genuine restorative power. Given to those fasting, those recovering from illness, and drunk on cold highland evenings.
ingredients: 600g fish — whole small fish or bone-in pieces
steps: Place fish in pot with cold water.
Bring to a gentle boil. Skim foam — 3 minutes.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, pepper, and cardamom.
Remove fish. Flake meat. Return to broth. Discard bones.
Season. Garnish with coriander. Serve with lime.
chefTips: Skim foam carefully — produces a cleaner broth.
Fish broth cooks much faster than meat broth — do not over-simmer.
The soup should be light golden from the turmeric.
commonMistakes: Over-cooking — fish falls apart and becomes mushy.
cookingScience: Fish produces gelatine from its collagen at lower temperatures and shorter times than meat — even 20 minutes of gentle simmering extracts significant gelatin from fish bones, producing a slightly body-rich broth. The inosinate (IMP) in fish also enhances umami perception in the broth.
sustainabilityTips: Whole fish or bony fish — maximum extraction from each catch.
servedWith: With injera for a light fasting meal
culturalNote: Fish soup is the fasting-period healing food of Ethiopia's lake communities — given to monks on their island monasteries, to fasting families in lakeside towns, and to anyone who needs nourishment without meat.
